r0.why: Molten or semi-molten source of all igneous rocks [1], beneath surface and incorrectly called lava [2], liquid rock with suspended crystals [9], gases bubble out near surface giving three phases [10].

r1.why: Melting of mantle or crust in the four listed settings [4], upward migration and thought storage in chambers or mush zones [5], feeds volcano as lava or solidifies as intrusion such as dike or sill [7].

r2.why: Mixture dominated by oxygen and silicon, most abundant crustal elements [12]; properties correlate with silica, four chemical types [14].

r3.why: Over 63% silica [15], viscosity figures for hot and cool rhyolite [17], water about 1 cP [18], explosive eruptions and fragmental deposits because of viscosity [19].

r4.why: 52-63% silica [24], 3.5 million cP at 1,200 C [27], peanut butter [28], mafic 52-45% [31], 1,100-1,200 C [32], 10^4-10^5 cP [33], ketchup [34], shield volcanoes and flood basalts [35].

r5.why: Extreme temperatures and komatiite as an ultramafic magma [39], under 45% silica [40], over 18% MgO and 1,600 C [41], 100-1000 cP like light motor oil [43], no modern komatiite as mantle cooled [45].

r6.why: All in [8]: study relied on lava flows; magma met in situ three times in geothermal drilling, twice Iceland, once Hawaii.
